title: Window Peaks
statement:
A security camera looks at **k** consecutive houses of a long street of **n** houses at a time. It starts at houses 1..k and moves one house to the right at every step until it shows houses n-k+1..n. At each position it reports the **tallest** house it sees.

Given the heights of the houses, print the **sum** of all the reported values (there are n - k + 1 of them).
input:
The first line contains two integers **n** and **k**.

The second line contains n integers h[1], ..., h[n].
output: Print one integer: the sum of the maximums of all windows of length k.

samples.explanation: The six windows are [1 3 1], [3 1 2], [1 2 4], [2 4 5], [4 5 3] and [5 3 6]. Their maximums are 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6 and the sum is 26.

hints: Looking at all k houses for every window costs O(n·k), too slow when k is about n / 2.
Keep a deque of indices whose heights are decreasing. Before adding house i, remove from the back all houses that are not taller than it: they can never be a maximum again.
The front of the deque is the maximum of the window. Remove it when it slides out of the window. The sum needs 64 bits.
editorial:
Monotonic deque. Keep indices in a deque so that their heights are strictly decreasing from front to back. For house i: pop from the back while the back height ≤ h[i], then push i. If the front index is ≤ i - k, it has left the window, so pop it from the front. When i ≥ k - 1, the front is the maximum of the window ending at i; add its height to the total. Every index enters and leaves the deque once.

Complexity: O(n).
